page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-180 is an x86_64 compute-heavy instance equipped with 180 dedicated vCPUs spanning 90 physical cores, driven by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. The system provides 354 GB of total system memory, resulting in an allocation of 1.97 GB per vCPU. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16, hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI cryptographic primitives, and BMI2 instructions. The server includes no onboard local storage drives and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation places this instance in the top 10 percent of cloud servers for raw multi-core throughput, reflected by a stress-ng multi-core score of 277,267.43, a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,894, and a PassMark CPU score of 124,714.88. High-concurrency operations show equal strength, demonstrated by Clang compilation scores reaching 71,002, Redis SET execution exceeding 211 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measuring 95.0 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth benchmarks record 13,631.91 GB/sec on cached small blocks and 346.92 GB/sec on uncached large reads. In machine learning benchmarks, prompt processing for small and medium language models reaches top-tier throughput via AVX-512 execution.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes high core density, maximizing CPU capacity per operational unit without allocating unnecessary memory overhead. The absence of local NVMe storage necessitates reliance on external network-attached block storage for persistent data, which should be factored into I/O architectural planning. Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-180 is strategically suited for parallelized software builds, continuous integration pipelines, multi-threaded scientific simulations, high-volume key-value caching, and CPU-driven inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-180 is a high-density compute instance featuring 180 dedicated vCPUs across 90 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors and paired with 354 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 instruction support, it delivers top-tier performance across multi-threaded computational benchmarks, including Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput Redis caching. With a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 2 GB per vCPU, the instance is structurally configured for compute-intensive tasks rather than memory-heavy datasets. The platform includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external storage volumes for stateful operations. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the high thread density provides effective compute utilization for parallelized workloads without paying for excess memory overhead. The c3d-highcpu-180 is engineered for large multi-threaded builds, distributed simulation, high-traffic static web serving, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
